pages.text: Steady magnets top out near 45 tesla. For more, dump a room of capacitors into a coil for a few milliseconds: $(thing)B = μ₀NI/L$().

The $(item)Pulsed Magnet Lab$() grows a storey for every stack of Bitter plates (1 to 7): more copper and cooling to soak up the pulse's heat (ΔT ∝ NI²t/storeys). Past 400 K the coil melts; past 100 T the magnetic pressure B²/2μ₀ tears it apart.
At 40 T it magnetises samarium-cobalt in bulk. At 80 T, with magnetar crust and cosmic ray shards, it searches for $(item)Magnetic Monopoles$() - and now and then, finds one.
